document_check.note: Document is Wang K, Shao B, Zeng Q, Liu X, Li K, Luo X. 'Trajectory of stratum radiatum, lacunosum and moleculare integrity in Alzheimer's disease continuum', Scientific Reports (2026) 16:5796. This matches 'Wang et al. 2026, P-595'. It is an ADNI (consortium) cross-sectional group comparison of hippocampal metrics (FreeSurfer 6.0 volumetry, ASHS subfields, visual MTA and SRLM ratings) across 178 CU A-, 91 CU A+, 90 MCI A+ and 14 AD A+ participants. It contains no radiomics or classifier analysis.

cited_result: Reduced hippocampal volume and higher visual hippocampal atrophy score in amyloid-positive MCI (n=90) than in amyloid-negative cognitively unimpaired controls (n=178), measured with FreeSurfer 6.0 volumetry and visual MTA rating (Table 2, p1 and p4-5). This is the only part of the cited sentence the document supports.
tool_reason: The cited result compares a biomarker (hippocampal volume or atrophy rating) between diagnostic groups at a single time point, so the JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist applies.

domains.domain: 1. Criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined
domains.rationale: The CU, MCI and dementia definitions and six exclusion criteria are stated explicitly.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) was defined following the criteria, which included preserved activities of daily living, the absence of dementia, objective cognitive impairment as demonstrated by the delayed recall test of the WMS-LM ... Exclusion criteria included: (1) absence of a PET-CT scan within one year of the structural MRI;

domains.domain: 2. Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The data source is ADNI, and demographics, cognition and biomarkers are tabulated by group. However, no recruitment period or selection flow (how the 373 were drawn from ADNI) is given.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: The data utilized in this study were obtained from the ADNI database. ... no significant differences were observed between the four groups in age (p = 0.066), sex distribution (p = 0.076), and vascular risk factors (VRF) (p = 0.789)

domains.domain: 3. Exposure (group membership) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Group membership combines clinical staging with amyloid PET status from the standard ADNI pipeline, using tracer-specific SUVR thresholds.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Amyloid positivity was determined based on summary SUVR thresholds (1.08 for FBB and 1.11 for FBP

domains.domain: 4. Objective, standard criteria for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: MCI is defined by standard ADNI criteria: WMS-LM delayed recall, CDR 0.5, preserved ADL and no dementia.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: objective cognitive impairment as demonstrated by the delayed recall test of the WMS-LM, and a CDR score of 0.5

domains.rationale: Age, sex and education are named as covariates, and the education imbalance is reported.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: MCI A+ and AD A+ showed relatively lower educational level than CU A-.

domains.domain: 6. Strategies to deal with confounding stated
domains.rationale: An adjusted ANCOVA is stated. Its results for the group comparison are only in a supplement that is not part of the document, and the main-text Table 2 p-values are unadjusted.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: Additionally, we conducted an ANCOVA, adjusting for age, sex, and education (Supplementary Material 1).

domains.rationale: Volume comes from the standard FreeSurfer 6.0 pipeline, normalised by ICV. Visual ratings were made by two raters blinded to diagnosis and age, with kappa 0.748.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: the visual hippocampal atrophy score was evaluated based on MTA by two individuals (KW, XL) who remained blinded to the participants' diagnoses and ages ... There were good agreements in the scores for the visual hippocampal atrophy score (Kappa = 0.748)

domains.rationale: The headline group comparisons are unadjusted one-way ANOVAs with LSD post hoc tests, repeated across more than 30 hippocampal metrics with no family-wise correction. Ordinal visual scores were treated as continuous. The adjusted ANCOVA results that would address the education imbalance are not reported in the document.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: Post hoc pairwise comparisons were subsequently performed to identify the source of significant differences detected by ANOVA, with results deemed significant at P < 0.05 using the least significant difference (LSD) method.

applicability.rationale: The MCI group is restricted to amyloid-positive MCI and compared with amyloid-negative controls. The sample is an ADNI subset with high-resolution coronal T2 imaging at 3 T and no reported selection flow, so the contrast is wider than an unselected MCI versus control comparison.

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: items 1 to 7 Yes, item 8 Unclear)
overall_rationale: Group definitions, measurement and confounder identification are sound, and hippocampal ratings were blinded with good inter-rater agreement. Under this review's rule the overall rating cannot be low, because the appropriateness of the analysis for the cited contrast is unclear. The main group tests are unadjusted despite lower education in MCI A+, the adjusted results are available only in an unseen supplement, and many metrics were tested with LSD only.
